verdict_rationale: Mandatory audit failure ALWAYS rolls back refund (K01, K02 prove it)
audit_logs is atomic (orphan rollback also verified)
No silent mandatory audit failure remains
Failure injection tests use real production flow with Schema::drop
IDOR clean (K04 proves payload spoofing is impossible)

files.issue: outer try/catch swallows RefundAuditLog::create() failure, returns null
inner try/catch swallows AuditLog::create() failure, continues silently

previous_vulnerability.consequence: Financial refund could commit while refund_audit_logs was silently lost

root_cause: RefundAuditLogger had a FAILURE POLICY docblock declaring it should NEVER throw to the caller. This conflicted with the audit requirement that refund MUST NOT commit unless mandatory audit row is persisted. The two policies were mutually exclusive; this fix adopts the strict requirement.

changes: Removed both try/catch blocks (outer at L59-131, inner at L96-121)
Changed return type from ?RefundAuditLog to RefundAuditLog
Actor identity from Auth::id() ONLY — $params['user_id'] ignored
Updated docblock with atomicity invariant and caller contract
Added Section K with 4 failure-injection tests
K01: refund_audit_logs drop → full rollback for Hajj
K02: audit_logs drop → full rollback including orphan refund_audit_logs row
K03: refund_audit_logs drop → full rollback for Visa
K04: actor spoofing via payload fields is ignored

transaction_boundary.before_fix: RefundAuditLogger swallowed exceptions → DB::transaction closure returned normally → COMMIT happened even if audit persistence failed
transaction_boundary.after_fix: RefundAuditLogger propagates exceptions → DB::transaction wrapper catches → ROLLBACK undoes all financial mutations

K01.what_was_mocked: Nothing. Schema::drop('refund_audit_logs') forces real RefundAuditLog::create() to throw QueryException
K01.why_real_transaction_boundary: Genuine PDOException from SQLite driver propagates through logRefund() (no catch) and triggers DB::transaction rollback

K02.what_was_mocked: Nothing. Schema::drop('audit_logs') forces second Eloquent insert to throw
K02.critical_scenario: refund_audit_logs succeeds first, then audit_logs fails. Orphan refund_audit_logs row must be rolled back.

K04.what_was_mocked: Nothing. Real HTTP POST with spoofed user_id/performed_by/actor_id/refund_audit payload fields
K04.verified: audit user_id = Auth::id() (normalEmployee), forged admin ID never appears, forged name 'Forged Admin' never appears

scope_safety.note: Pre-existing Bus modifications were already present at conversation start (visible in initial gitStatus snapshot). They are NOT introduced by this atomicity fix and are explicitly out of scope per the spec.
